chunks: And from his sayings (peace be upon him), he said:

To Abdullah ibn al-Abbas, who had brought him a letter from Uthman while he was besieged, asking him to leave for his estate in Yanbu' so that the people's clamor for his caliphate would subside, after he had previously asked him for the same. He (peace be upon him) said:

key_terms.بَيْنُوب: Yanbu', a coastal city where Ali owned an estate
key_terms.عُثْمَان: Uthman ibn Affan, the third Rashidun Caliph
key_terms.مُحْصَر: Besieged (referring to Uthman's house in Medina)

ai.seo_question: What did Uthman ask Imam Ali to do during his siege to calm the public demand for his caliphate?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha highlights the political tension during Uthman's siege, where he sought Imam Ali's neutrality to quell the growing public demand for his leadership. Historically, this reflects the strategic dilemma faced by the Umayyad caliphate, which viewed Ali's prestige as both a stabilizing force and a potential threat to their authority. The incident underscores the early Shia perspective on the legitimacy of the Prophet's family versus the emerging Umayyad political structure.

en.sayed-ali-raza: When ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān was surrounded, ‘Abdullāh ibn al-‘Abbās brought a letter to Amīr al-mu’minīn from ‘Uthmān in which he expressed the desire that Amīr al-mu’minīn should leave for his estate Yanbu‘ so that the proposal that was being mooted out for him to become caliph should subside. ‘Uthmān had this request earlier also.
